---
title: "Missing values and sample accounting"
---

Every model function defaults to listwise deletion: a row with a missing value
in any variable the model uses is left out of the fit. For the formula
functions these are the variables the formula references, including weights,
offsets and grouping factors; other columns may contain missing values. For the
matrix functions they are the supplied predictors, outcome, weights, offsets
and groups. The `missing` argument selects the policy:

```php
$result = Phit\fit_ols(x: $x, y: $y); // missing: 'drop'
$result = Phit\fit_ols(x: $x, y: $y, missing: 'raise'); // reject missing values
```

## What counts as missing

PHP null and floating-point NAN represent missing values. Positive and negative
infinity are invalid numerical input, not missingness. Strings (including empty
strings and 'NA'), booleans, objects and absent/ragged matrix elements remain
errors. Numeric zero is a valid value. No value is imputed or coerced from text.

Validation inspects all original values and shapes before deletion. A missing
value cannot hide an invalid value or ragged row. After deletion, the retained
fixed design must still have n > p (including the automatically added intercept) and full numerical rank. If no usable fit remains,
the call throws. The Rust fit_ols() contract continues to require complete finite
numeric vectors; the PHP binding implements the omission policy before calling it.

## Warning and accounting

Every successful fit that omits observations emits one native PHP E_WARNING
including the number dropped and original sample size. Complete data emits no
warning. missing: 'raise' throws when missing values are found, without fitting.
An unsuccessful fit throws rather than returning deletion metadata. Warning text
is descriptive and is not a stable machine-readable interface.

Every successful result also includes:

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| n_input | int: original observations |
| n_observations | int: retained observations used in estimation |
| n_dropped | int: omitted observations |
| retained_rows | list<int>: original zero-based iteration positions retained |
| dropped_rows | list<int>: original zero-based iteration positions omitted |

These positions refer to input iteration order, not PHP array keys. Each list is
in ascending original order. fitted and residuals contain retained observations
only, in retained_rows order; they are not padded with null. All statistics use
the retained sample, including df_residual = n_observations - p. Metadata remains
available even if warning display is disabled by PHP configuration.

```php
foreach ($result['retained_rows'] as $outputPosition => $inputPosition) {
    $residualForOriginalPosition[$inputPosition] = $result['residuals'][$outputPosition];
}
```

Applications should use their normal warning handling to log or display the
message and use the structured counts for reporting. PHP error handlers that
promote warnings to exceptions can abort this call; use missing: 'raise' when
omission should be prohibited explicitly. Warnings may be suppressed by PHP
settings, so user-facing applications should also inspect n_dropped rather than
rely only on display_errors. Do not suppress deletion without recording it.

## Statistical interpretation and reference behavior

Listwise deletion is simple and preserves aligned observations, but changes the
estimation sample. It does not guarantee unbiased results for arbitrary missingness.
Report the excluded count and investigate why values are missing; this policy
implements neither imputation nor a missing-data model.

R's explicit [na.action = na.omit](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/lm.html)
and statsmodels' explicit [missing='drop'](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/missing.html)
provide comparable complete-case fits. Do not assume that every reference library
warns on omission by default: warnings and metadata are our explicit contract.
The [three implementation verification](verifications/ols.qmd) checks identical
retained samples and numerical results, with the PHP warning captured as evidence.

This changes the initial API, which rejected null and NAN. Existing callers that
need that strict behavior should pass missing: 'raise'. Other invalid inputs
continue to be rejected. Helpers can still perform their own explicit preparation;
when they omit data before the call, they must report it themselves because the
extension can account only for rows it actually receives.

## Logistic outcomes

`fit_logistic()` follows the same deletion, warning and row-accounting policy
as `fit_ols()`. With default unit trial weights, numeric outcomes must be exactly 0 or 1, including rows with
missing predictors. After deletion both classes must remain and n must exceed p;
otherwise fitting fails. Its residuals are response residuals y - probability,
and both residuals and fitted probabilities follow retained_rows order.

## Probit and Poisson outcomes

Probit follows the binary rules above. Poisson validates nonnegative integer
counts before deletion; after deletion at least one positive count must remain.
All estimators warn once on a successful fit that dropped rows, expose original
row positions, and support missing: 'raise'. Zero Poisson counts are observed
values, not missingness. Returned mean counts and residuals follow retained_rows.

## Mixed-model group IDs

fit_mixed_intercept() deletes a row if x, y or the group ID is missing. Group missingness
means null; NAN/float group IDs are invalid categorical labels and are rejected.
Validation still covers every original value before deletion. Group labels and
sizes describe the retained sample, and groups completely removed by deletion
are absent from results. If deletion leaves only one group, all singletons or
insufficient fixed-design observations, fitting fails. Inspect retained_rows to
align conditional/population fits and both residual definitions with original data.

## Expanded inputs

Optional weights/offsets and every random term's z/groups participate in the same
listwise deletion mask. Validate original lengths, types and values before
deletion; preserve aligned rows across all vectors and terms. The fixed-model
contracts now permit grouped-binomial proportions with positive integer trial
weights. Invalid success/trial counts remain errors, even in rows that would
otherwise be dropped. General mixed fits return one warning and original row
positions just like the existing functions. These cases are tested in
`tests/r-compatibility.php` and `tests/lmm-expanded.php`.

`fit_logistic_mixed` applies the same policy across x, proportions, groups,
trial counts and offsets. Trial counts above 1,000,000 are rejected before
deleting rows. Near-integer success encodings within tolerance are canonicalized
only after original validation and deletion; zero-success/zero-failure samples
then fail as required for a finite unpenalized fit.
